conventions.convention: The coordinate inner product is linear in the first argument. Ancillas precede the system, and the all-zero block is B_U=J_a†UJ_a.

A block encoding requires α>0, α≥‖A‖, and normalized error ‖B_U−Â/α‖≤ε. The corresponding unnormalized tolerance is αε; the normalization promise is additional to the cited source's approximate convention.
Rectangular matrices use declared isometric embeddings and Â=E_out A E_in† on a common positive-dimensional system space; square matrices use identity embeddings.

Forward, inverse, controlled, and controlled-inverse operations are separate access capabilities. SELECT may be supplied or assembled, with its controls, phases, preparation, synthesis, data access, and classical costs charged explicitly.
The product construction uses separate ancillas in A-ancilla, B-ancilla, system order and returns V_A V_B, applying B first without intermediate measurement or reset.
LCU inputs have exact component encodings and nonzero coefficients after zero coefficients are omitted. Λ=Σ|β_j|α_j>0; PREPARE amplitudes are √(|β_j|α_j/Λ), and SELECT carries β_j/|β_j|.

load_bearing.statement: For α>0 and ε≥0, a block encoding requires α≥‖A‖op and ‖B_U−Â/α‖op≤ε, where B_U=J_a†UJ_a and Â=E_out A E_in†.

An access instance records each supplied forward, inverse, controlled, and controlled-inverse operation separately, including whether SELECT is supplied or assembled; a call to one operation does not imply access to another.

Under the product algorithm's square-matrix inputs and separate-ancilla order, the all-zero block is C_A C_B. Its normalized error is at most ε_A‖B‖/α_B+ε_B‖A‖/α_A+ε_Aε_B; the sharper bound ε_B+ε_A‖B‖/α_B≤ε_A+ε_B also holds.
Under the exact LCU inputs and instructions, the all-zero coefficient and component-ancilla block is (Σβ_j A_j)/Λ, and ‖Σβ_j A_j‖op≤Λ; hence the construction is a (Λ,b+a_*,0) block encoding.

For a finite system space, an ancilla injection J_a x=e_0⊗x, and a unitary U on the joint space, B_U=J_a†UJ_a satisfies ‖B_U‖op≤1. Consequently every exact (α,a,0) block encoding of A satisfies ‖A‖op≤α.

concerns.concern: F1 says 'in the exact case $B_U=A/\alpha$' and Proof 2.1 says '$A=\alpha B_U$'. The Statement covers every exact encoding under def-qa-22-block-encoding, including rectangular targets, for which B_U is d×d and A is m×n. The cited definition instead gives B_U=Â/α. The conclusion is sound, but the proof needs the padding norm identity ‖Â‖=‖A‖ already proved in the definition, rather than the dimensionally invalid equality.

alerts.finding: Facts F5 attributes to def-qc-dirac-notation-conversion: '$|u\rangle\langle v|$ contributes the matrix entry $\langle e_i,u\rangle\langle v,e_j\rangle$ in the stated basis convention.' With the declared root-linear-first pairing this is the conjugate of the correct entry: the supplier defines the matrix as [u][v]†. For u=i e_i and v=e_j, the quoted expression gives −i while the actual entry is i. Proof 2.1 itself uses the correct root pairing order for U_L†U_R, so this finding concerns the false cited fact rather than that computation.

seams_checked.note: The access model retains full-description generator time and separate quantum, classical, oracle, and precision coordinates; it asserts no uniform synthesis from matrix data.

The optional LCU preparation preserves the exact-table and ideal continuous-angle hypotheses, charges workspace and table scanning, and explicitly explains why the positive reference amplitude removes the supplier's ray-versus-vector phase ambiguity.
Positive-dimensional registers, all-zero injections, ordered factors, and identity padding agree with the register and tensor definitions.
Product and LCU operator products use the supplier's rightmost-first chronology and introduce no measurement or reset.
The owned items consistently use the root-linear-first convention and Dirac conversion; LCU coefficient phases enter SELECT without unintended conjugation.
Controlled and inverse calls remain separate capabilities; relative component phases are included in SELECT and its costs.
The LCU remark correctly distinguishes a unitary-valued SELECT from the supplier's XOR-valued function oracle and requires explicit implementation.
The PUE definition identifies exact square block encodings as a special case. The robustness theorem explicitly retains declared rectangular padding, normalized input error, and α≥‖A‖.

The qubitization access model uses exact compression K/α without requiring U itself to be Hermitian. Sparse constructions separately establish their normalization bounds and charge inverse and controlled access. The unrelated Dirac fact defect is preserved in alerts.

QLSP retains normalized block error and explicit access. Its conditional LCU identity uses weights |β_j|α_j/Λ and SELECT phases β_j/|β_j|; the Fourier construction explicitly accounts for preparation and component workspace.

The normalized-function lemma supplies the required target norm bound. The matrix-function construction uses unit component scales and normalization Σγ_j, and its error proof applies LCU to the actual component compressions with implementation deviations charged separately.

The Fourier and Gibbs constructions use normalized finite coefficient sums, explicit preparation and SELECT operations, and declared implementation errors; normalization dilution and matrix perturbation are accounted for separately.
